newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Police chief transferred in Philippine rape case.
newsitem.headline: Police chief transferred in Philippine rape case.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Saturday removed from his post a senior police officer who had said a fugitive legislator charged with the statutory rape of an 11-year-old girl had fled to Indonesia.

Romeo Jalosjos, a member of Ramos' coalition in the House of Representatives, was captured by soldiers on an islet 60 km from Manila on Friday. He was on the run for 23 days after a court ordered him arrested.
The police officer posted in the southern Philippines, where Jalosjos was the congressman, had told reporters he was "99.9 percent sure" the lawmaker was in Indonesia.
Ramos ordered "the relief of Police Chief Superintendent Manuel Pepino for 'unprofessional conduct' in connection with the Jalosjos case," a presidential palace news release said.
It said investigators "suspected that Pepino's statement was calculated to throw them off Jalosjos' trail."

Pepino's remarks had led the foreign affairs department to seek Jakarta's help in locating Jalosjos and Indonesia's Antara news agency said authorities in North Sulawesi had begun distributing pictures of him.
A judge ordered Jalosjos' arrest on December 26 on two counts of statutory rape and 12 counts of acts of lasciviousness.
Jalosjos has denied allegations by the girl that he had sex with her several times in his Manila apartment last year after paying up to 10,000 pesos ($385) each time.

Following his arrest on Friday by the elite Presidential Security Guard (PSG), Jalosjos repeated his previous statements that he had been unjustly tried in the media. "There's only one victim in this case and that is me," he said.
Ramos had personally ordered the PSG to hunt down Jalosjos and the arrest came after a dramatic operation involving six helicopters encircling the island house where he stayed.
PSG chief Jose Calimlim said Jalosjos had drawn up an elaborate escape plan using a helicopter, a light plane and a boat to Malaysia from where he planned to flee to London.
Jalosjos' lawyers denied the lawmaker was hiding and said he was waiting for the results of a petition before an appeals court to quash the arrest warrant.
Police failure to arrest Jalosjos had caused a public uproar with newspapers saying this was yet another example of the rich and powerful being immune from the law.
Jalosjos was produced before Makati Regional Trial Court Judge Roberto Diokno who ordered him jailed for the entire period of the trial.
A hand-cuffed Jalosjos was taken to the Makati jail where he was alloted a cell with six other inmates and jail guards said they were very happy to receive an important prisoner.
The Philippine Daily Inquirer newspaper said the jail warden had ordered inmates to clean up their cells as he expected a stream of visitors including the media.
